legendre_split_identity: ((P-1)^2,P^2)=((P-1)^2,P^2-P] union (P^2-P,P^2), with P-1 integers in each half.
plain_conclusion: The top strict row is exactly the prime-indexed Oppermann left half. A C=1 right-endpoint square-root theorem at X=P^2 is precisely the needed top-row input, while Legendre's wider interval splits into a lower leak half and the target half. Thus Legendre-scale or any fixed C>1 square-root input cannot by itself close the row/column theorem.
prime_endpoint_note: Both endpoints P^2-P and P^2 are composite, so any prime in the closed C=1 interval lies in the open top row.
